crop: Sweet pepper / bell pepper / poivron (Capsicum annuum, blocky types e.g. Yolo Wonder, California Wonder), open field
pilot_zone_context: Foumbot (Noun, West Cameroon), Bamoun plateau ~1,000-1,200 m, volcanic soils, single rainy season mid-March to mid-November, dry season mid-November to mid-March (P4). Foumbot growers: Yolo Wonder used by 55% and Simba by 45% of surveyed farmers; Lamuyo F1 also cited; 89% farm 0.5-1 ha; 80% grow pepper twice a year (P4).

detail.where: Foumbot farmer practice (~1.5 months) and Kenya (about 45 days)
Cameroon IFATI sheet (1-2 months, 5-6 leaf stage, ~10 cm)

germination_days.note: 8 days at 25-35 degC, 13 days at 20 degC, 25 days at 15 degC; none below 15 or above 35 degC (P1); ~2 weeks (P3); ~10 days (P13)

transplant_to_first_flower_days.note: ~1 month (P13); Foumbot trial transplanted 24 May 2020, first flowers 28 July 2020 = 65 days (P5)

flowering_to_first_harvest_days.note: 35-40 days to optimum harvest (P1); 35-50 days to mature green (P6)

detail.where: Kenya SHEP (75 d green, ~90 d coloured)

detail.note: ~10 weeks open field for Commandant F1 (Kenya)

harvest_frequency.text: About twice a week (P13); fruits picked as they reach full size and firmness (P1); Foumbot growers harvest more than three times per cycle (P4).

total_cycle_days.notes: Stated: ~5.5 months (~165 days) seed to end (P13); 'four months' (P11). Range is analyst sum of component ranges: nursery 21-56 + transplant-to-harvest 60-90 + open-field harvest 42-70 days.

crops_per_year.text: 80% of Foumbot pepper farmers grow it twice a year; most prefer the rainy season, some grow year-round where irrigation (canals, motor pumps) is available (P4).

spacing.layout: 1 m between rows x 0.5 m in row on 1 m beds; 200 plants per 100 m2 (Cameroon IFATI)
1.5 m beds (furrow to furrow), 30 cm high, 2 rows 55 cm apart, plants 45 cm apart (AVRDC)
60 x 45 cm or 70 x 30 cm by variety (Kenya SHEP); 14,814-19,047 plants/acre
75 x 45 cm (Kenya expert; text states 10,000 plants/ha, inconsistent with the spacing)
rows 1 m x 0.6 m in row large varieties; 45 cm in row small varieties (St Lucia)
single rows 1 m x 50 cm, or double rows (1.2-1.5 m between pairs, 30-50 cm between lines, 40-50 cm in line)
Foumbot/Bangou trial: 1 m wide, 20 cm high beds, 3 rows, 30 x 30 cm

detail.note: ~130 seeds/g, for 30,000 plants/ha at 90% germination and survival
nursery seed rate 0.5 kg/ha (1 kg/ha if direct sown)

nursery.text: Raised beds 1-1.2 m wide (P2, P3), drills 10-20 cm apart (P2), seed 1 cm deep every 2 cm (P3); compost/manure 2-3 kg/m2 in nursery (P6); shade then harden 1-2 weeks (P2) or 4-5 days (P1); insect-proof netting against whitefly (P2). In Foumbot 79% raise seedlings on ridges, 21% on seedbeds; seeds untreated, nursery sprayed every 1-2 weeks from about one week after emergence (P4).

nursery_area_m2_per_ha.notes: Derived, not stated for sweet pepper: Foumbot trial used 2 g seed on 2 m2 (1 g/m2), so 300 g/ha needs ~300 m2 (P5); Benin hot-pepper sheet uses a 4 m2 nursery for 400 m2 of field, i.e. ~100 m2/ha (P23).

staking.text: Stake within one month after transplanting (P3). Most varieties need staking (P1). Stakes every 1.5 m with 2-3 levels of wire/string (P13); trellis stakes 2 m apart (P12). Stake quantities per ha and costs: not found.

transplanting.text: 4-6 true leaves, early morning or late evening (P2); 5-6 leaves, ~10 cm (P3); 8-10 true leaves, ~20 cm (P13). Bury to half plant height (P1).

seed_price.notes: No Cameroonian seed price found. Kenya: F1 'Green Bell' seed cost KSh 120,000 per acre (P11, low confidence).

itinerary.description: Sow on raised beds or trays (see planting.nursery). Feed seedlings with 0.25% 10-10-10 solution at 2 true leaves (P1). Damping-off: metalaxyl + mancozeb (P2) or 0.25% benomyl drench (P1; benomyl withdrawn in many countries). Harden off before transplanting (P1, P2). Foumbot practice: nursery sprayed every 1-2 weeks (P4).

inputs.product: Sweet pepper seed (OPV Yolo Wonder / California Wonder or F1)

itinerary.description: No Solanaceae (tomato, potato, eggplant) for at least 3 years (P2, P6); rotations of 3-5 years cited (P6); rotation with rice recommended, avoid potato, tomato, sweet potato (P1). Soil pH 6.5-7 (P3); 5.5-6.8 (P6); 6.0-6.5 (P9).

itinerary.step: Land clearing and pre-plant weed control
itinerary.description: Glyphosate burndown at least 15 days before planting: 250 ml Glyfos per 1,000 m2 (~2.5 L/ha) (P13); Round-up about 2 weeks before transplanting (P12). Foumbot farmers use glyphosate (50%), paraquat (37%) and 2,4-D (23%), 2-3 herbicide applications per cycle (P4); paraquat is banned in many jurisdictions, check Cameroon homologation list. Stale seedbed: shallow tillage 3-5 cm (P13). Slash-and-burn: no source found documenting or quantifying it for pepper in Foumbot (gap).

Deep ploughing to 30 cm about one month before transplanting, beds 1 m wide (P3); ploughing 30-35 cm (P13); beds 1.5 m wide, 30 cm high (P1). Mulch option: rice straw 5 t/ha or plastic mulch laid before transplanting (P1).

At least 2 kg well-decomposed manure per planting hole (P3), i.e. ~40 t/ha at 20,000 plants/ha (analyst calculation). Kenya: 10 t/ha manure (P9); Kenya chilli 15 t/ha (P6). French Polynesia: 4-5 t per 1,000 m2 (40-50 t/ha, unusually high) (P13). Foumbot trial used poultry droppings with NPK 20-10-10, rate not given (P5).

Cameroon IFATI: NPK 11-22-16 or 12-14-19 at 22 g per hole + potassium sulphate 8 g per hole, ~5 days before transplanting (document also says 15-30 days; inconsistent) (P3); at 20,000 plants/ha this equals ~440 kg/ha NPK + ~160 kg/ha K2SO4 (analyst calc). AVRDC: 40% of N and 50% of P and K basal (P1). Kenya SHEP: 100 kg/acre DAP or TSP (~247 kg/ha) mixed into soil (P2). St Lucia: 450 kg/ha 12-12-17+2 at planting (P12).

Transplant at 4-6 true leaves (P2) / 5-6 leaves ~10 cm (P3), early morning or evening; spacing per planting.spacing. AVRDC also cites carbofuran granules in the hole (P1); carbofuran is banned in many countries and is not recommended here.

Total 600-800 mm per cycle (~400 mm vegetative, 200-400 mm reproductive); soil moisture 80-85% for good yields (P3). ~2 mm/day early, 3-6 mm/day from flowering to harvest, preferably morning (P13). Irrigate when available soil moisture falls to 40-50%; furrow or drip, avoid sprinklers and evening overhead watering (P1). 1-2 times a week, every two days in hot dry weather (P6). Foumbot: surface canals from mountain streams, motor pumps on farms >0.25 ha, watering cans on small plots (P4).

inputs.unit: m3 per cycle (600-800 mm total crop need, midpoint; rainfall counts toward it)

itinerary.description: Stake within one month after transplanting (P3); stakes every 1.5 m with 2-3 wire levels (P13).

inputs.unit: quantity not given in sources (1 stake per 1.5 m of row per P13)

itinerary.description: AVRDC: first of three equal N side-dressings (60% of N) at 2 weeks after transplanting (P1). Kenya SHEP: CAN 40 kg/acre (~99 kg/ha, 5 g/hole) at 2-3 weeks (P2). French Polynesia: 12-12-17 200 kg/ha + urea 50 kg/ha + K2SO4 60 kg/ha at transplant +15 days (P13). Foumbot practice: NPK 20-10-10, a handful per 1-2 plants, from one or two weeks after transplanting (P4).

AVRDC: second N side-dressing at 4 WAT plus remaining 50% of P and K (P1). Kenya SHEP: CAN 80 kg/acre (~198 kg/ha, 10 g/hole) at 4-6 weeks (P2). Polynesia: 12-12-17 90 kg/ha + K2SO4 80 kg/ha at +30 days (P13). Cameroon IFATI at flowering (~40 days after transplanting): per plant 15 g NPK 11-22-16 + 20 g K2SO4 + 2 g urea, i.e. ~300 kg NPK + 400 kg K2SO4 + 40 kg urea per ha at 20,000 plants (analyst calc) (P3). Avoid high N during flowering (P2).

AVRDC: third N side-dressing at 6 WAT (P1). Polynesia: 12-12-17 50 kg/ha + urea 30 kg/ha at +45 days (P13). St Lucia: side-dress every 4-6 weeks with 225 kg/ha CAN or 12-12-17 (P12). Foumbot practice: NPK 20-10-10 every 21 days and after each harvest (48% of farmers) (P4).

Foumbot: main foliar fertiliser is NPK 30-10-10, rate not reported (P4). Blossom-end rot prevention: lime, calcium nitrate, dolomite or gypsum and regular watering; calcium chloride spray cited with mancozeb against leaf spot (P2). No calcium foliar rate for open-field sweet pepper found (gap).

Weeding every two weeks until flowering (Foumbot/Bangou trial practice, P5). Post-transplant herbicide options in a tropical sheet: fluazifop-P-butyl 150 ml per 1,000 m2 (PHI 35 d), quizalofop-P-ethyl (PHI 21 d) (P13).
Remove fruits set at the first bifurcation node and all leaves and branches below it (P1, P6); keep 3 branches and ~10 fruits per plant (P13). Dip knives in 3% trisodium phosphate or milk (P1, P6).

Scout at least twice a week (60 random plants per 0.1 ha) (P1, P6). Foumbot practice: 85% of farmers use synthetic pesticides, weekly insecticide and fungicide sprays adjusted to disease severity; cypermethrin = 63% of insecticide active ingredients, mancozeb = 85% of fungicide AIs; harvest 1-7 days after last spray (P4). West Cameroon survey for poivron: chlorpyrifos (Dursban 4E 15 ml/15 L 1-2 times a month; Greforce 480 EC 15 ml per knapsack weekly), mancozeb, chlorothalonil + carbendazim, copper oxide + metalaxyl (P7); chlorpyrifos is banned in Cameroon and the EU (P27). Cameroon IFATI: maneb or mancozeb, dimethoate for aphids (P3). See pests_diseases for targets. Typical PHI 15 days minimum for insecticides/fungicides in the Polynesian sheet (P13). Spray volume ~800 L/ha (P13). Rotate at least three modes of action (P1).

inputs.unit: rate not reported in Cameroon sources
10 ml per 15 L knapsack cited for pepper (P7)

inputs.product: Metalaxyl + copper (e.g. Ridomil Gold Plus / Plantomil)

inputs.unit: L product (20 ml Success 4 per 1,000 m2)
kg product for aphids (25 g/1,000 m2); 0.5 kg for whitefly (50 g/1,000 m2)

itinerary.description: Start ~60-90 days after transplanting at mature-green stage (P2, P3, P13); harvest at full size and firmness before colour change unless coloured fruit is targeted (P1); green fruit does not ripen after picking (P2). Pick about twice a week (P13), early morning with clean knife or scissors (P2).

Sort out defective fruit, grade by colour, maturity, shape and size, pack in plastic crates, keep cool, shaded, ventilated and away from ethylene sources (P2). Storage 1-4 weeks at 7-10 degC (P13). Foumbot growers store 7-15 days after harvest (P4). Local sale unit in Bafou (West Cameroon): lots of 8-10 kg (P16); Yaounde retail by heaps (tas) or by count (P15).

recommendations.name: AVRDC (target 28 t/ha, no soil supply assumed)
recommendations.note: Reported as N, P, K (elemental per source wording; if elemental, ~229 kg P2O5 and ~193 kg K2O). Crop needs N 70, P 10, K 80 kg/ha. Reduce by soil test.

recommendations.name: French Polynesia / CIRAD Ferti-Run (needs for 10 t/ha)
recommendations.note: Schedule totals are analyst arithmetic from the 12-12-17 + urea + K2SO4 plan

recommendations.name: Cameroon IFATI (derived at 20,000 plants/ha)
recommendations.note: Analyst arithmetic: 740 kg NPK 11-22-16 + 560 kg K2SO4 (assumed 50% K2O) + 40 kg urea. K appears very high; verify with IRAD.

recommendations.name: Kenya SHEP (derived)
recommendations.note: Analyst arithmetic: 247 kg DAP + 297 kg CAN (assumed 26% N). No K.

fertilizer_total.foumbot_practice: NPK 20-10-10 by handful (no kg/ha), foliar NPK 30-10-10 (P4).
fertilizer_total.notes: No IRAD-validated recommendation for Foumbot volcanic soils was found.

pests_diseases.name: Whiteflies (Bemisia) and virus vectors
pests_diseases.controls: Lambda-cyhalothrin + thiamethoxam, insect netting, yellow traps (P2); acetamiprid, pyriproxyfen (P13); avoid planting next to tomato (P1 rotation logic)

pests_diseases.name: Fruit borers (Helicoverpa etc.)
pests_diseases.controls: Lambda-cyhalothrin, Bt, neem, hand-picking, trap crop (P2)

pests_diseases.name: Fruit flies
pests_diseases.controls: Cyromazine, spinosad, methyl-eugenol (16/ha) and cue-lure (32/ha) traps (P13)

pests_diseases.name: Cutworms
pests_diseases.controls: Azadirachtin, imidacloprid (P2); treat if >=1% seedlings cut (P6)

pests_diseases.name: Bacterial spot (Xanthomonas)
pests_diseases.controls: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb; mancozeb + fixed copper (P1)

pests_diseases.name: Phytophthora blight (P. capsici)
pests_diseases.controls: Metalaxyl, fixed copper (P1); drainage, raised beds

pests_diseases.name: Cercospora leaf spot
pests_diseases.controls: Azoxystrobin; copper hydroxide/sulphate; mancozeb + calcium chloride spray (P2, P13)

pests_diseases.name: Viruses (TMV, CMV and others)
pests_diseases.controls: Rogueing, oil sprays, reflective mulch, vector control (P2)

pests_diseases.name: Blossom-end rot
pests_diseases.controls: Lime, calcium nitrate, dolomite, gypsum, regular watering (P2)

foumbot_reported_problems: Diseases named by Foumbot growers: mildew, cercospora, phytophthora blight, fusarium wilt, anthracnose, ripe rot, TMV, CMV, galls; pests: flea beetles, cutworms, aphids, weevils, caterpillars, grasshoppers, pepper maggots, leaf miners. 85% could not identify pests/diseases; respondents report disease-related yield loss above 50% (P4). West Cameroon pepper growers' loss estimates: 36% report 0-25%, 21% 25-50%, 33% 50-75%, 10% 75-100% (P7).

sprays_per_cycle.notes: Not reported as a count. Foumbot: weekly insecticide and fungicide sprays (P4), so roughly one spray per week of field time (~16-20 over a 4-5 month field period, analyst inference).

labour_notes: No person-day budget for sweet pepper found. Comparators only: South Africa chillies (10 t/ha) 1,900 h harvesting + 1,102 h packing per ha (P25); Nigeria Delta State pepper, weeding 9 man-days per acre (P21); Ghana Upper East chilli labour costed only in cedis (P20). Cameroon wage reference: 500-2,000 FCFA/person-day (2005, Bamboutos) (P16).

national_or_regional_average.where: Cameroon, FAOSTAT 'Chillies and peppers, green' (21,345 hg/ha; 2.14 t/ha in 2022). Includes hot peppers; likely FAO-imputed.

farmer_rainfed.notes: Cameroon IFATI technical sheet: 5-7 t/ha (5-7 kg per 10 m2) (P3); FAOSTAT national 2.1 t/ha (P14). Foumbot survey gives output per farm (86% harvest 0.5-20 t/yr) but no t/ha (P4).

good_practice_rainfed.notes: Ghana open-field trial (Kade, minor season 2014-15): Yolo Wonder 7.53, California Wonder 12.57, range of 9 varieties 5.02-12.57 t/ha (P8). Kenya SHEP: OPV California/Yolo Wonder 6,000 kg/acre = 14.8 t/ha (P2).

irrigated_dry_season.notes: Polynesia target 10 t/ha (P13); St Lucia 20-22.5 t/ha (P12); AVRDC target 28 t/ha (P1); Kenya blog 5-8 t/acre (12.4-19.8 t/ha), up to 10 t/acre (24.7 t/ha) with irrigation (P10). Seed-company-type claims for F1 Commandant/Admiral open field 25-30 t/acre (62-74 t/ha) (P2) and 25-30 t/acre (P11) are treated as non-representative.

fruit_count_basis.text: Kenya: 10,000 plants/ha x 15-25 marketable fruits = 150,000-250,000 fruits/ha (P9).

post_harvest_loss_pct.notes: No measured post-harvest loss % found for sweet pepper in Cameroon or the region. Pre-harvest disease losses reported >50% by Foumbot respondents (P4). Shelf life 7-15 days in Foumbot practice (P4), 1-4 weeks at 7-10 degC (P13).

prices.unit_notes: Cameroon sells pepper by heap (tas), by count, by 8-10 kg lot or sack; per-kg values are computed only when the source gives a weight. Non-FCFA prices kept in original currency.

observations.market: Bafou, Bamboutos highlands (West Cameroon), producer/local market
observations.notes: 1,300-2,000 FCFA per 8-10 kg (per-kg = analyst division). Publication 2005, data possibly older.

observations.price_per_unit: 200 FCFA for 5 large peppers; heap 200-500 FCFA by size

observations.notes: Peppers among vegetables with sharpest monthly increase; vegetables index +12.9% y/y. No unit price.

observations.market: Upper East Ghana, chilli (not sweet pepper)

prices.seasonality: West Cameroon (Bafou): pepper prices higher in the dry season than the wet season (P16). Yaounde: vegetables more abundant in rainy season (P26); Mfoundi abundant mid-August 2021 (P15); national pepper prices rose sharply in September-October 2025 (P17, P18). Kenya: peak 80-150 vs off-peak 40-60 KSh/kg (P10). Implication (inference): dry-season irrigated production in Foumbot should capture higher prices.

cost_of_production_xaf_per_ha.notes: No Cameroonian sweet-pepper cost-of-production budget found. Gap.
Low confidence; ranges given per item.

temperature.fruit_growth_stops: RH below 60% combined with high temperature (P3)

climate.humidity_rain: Anthracnose infects above 70% RH, optimum 27 degC (P6); bacterial wilt favoured by 29.7-35.3 degC (P6); whitefly/virus vectors favoured by 25-30 degC dry conditions (P6). Avoid overhead and evening irrigation (P1). Foumbot growers report disease losses >50% (P4); phytophthora and anthracnose favoured by wet season (inference consistent with P6 thresholds).

planting_windows.sourced: Foumbot: most growers plant in the rainy season (mid-March to mid-November); 80% grow two crops a year; irrigated growers produce year-round (P4). Research trial transplanted late May 2020 at Foumbot (P5). French Polynesia sows February-June for the cooler season (P13), illustrating the preference for cooler months.
planting_windows.analyst_inference_not_sourced: For Foumbot: (a) nursery February-March, transplant at onset of rains (late March-April), harvest June-August; (b) nursery late August-September, transplant September-October, harvest December-February in the dry season with irrigation, which sources suggest coincides with higher prices (P16) and lower foliar disease pressure. Validate with station temperature data (not retrieved).

confidence_notes: MEDIUM for agronomy: Cameroon-specific references exist (IFATI sheet P3, Foumbot farmer survey P4, Foumbot trial P5) and agree broadly with AVRDC/SHEP/tropical sheets on nursery 4-8 weeks, 20,000-30,000 plants/ha, ~300 g seed/ha, first harvest 60-90 DAT, temperature optimum 21-24 degC. Fertiliser totals vary widely (N 75-175, K2O 0-398 kg/ha) and the Cameroonian IFATI per-plant doses imply very high K; needs IRAD soil-based validation. LOW for economics: no Cameroonian t/ha survey yield, cost of production, margin or labour budget for sweet pepper was found; Cameroonian price data are a 2005 Bafou per-lot price (130-313 FCFA/kg) and a 2021 Yaounde per-count price; the 2026 aggregator price (2,096-3,893 FCFA/kg retail) is unverified. Ghanaian/Nigerian margin studies concern mostly chilli. Gaps: Foumbot farm-gate price per kg by season and sale unit weight (sac/filet/cageot), cost of production, labour person-days, post-harvest loss %, calcium/foliar rates, sprays per cycle count, Foumbot temperature series. FAOSTAT API, several French sites and HAL were blocked, and the shared web-search budget ran out before Technisem/Tropicasem guides and further Cameroon market articles could be searched.
